```{r, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
library(ChAMP)
library(ChAMPdata)
library(matrixStats)
library(pheatmap)
library(dendextend)
library(dplyr)
library(minfi)
library(scales)
library(Hmisc)

data_storage_folder = "../../../Data/Processed/Huang"
if (!file.exists(data_storage_folder)) dir.create(data_storage_folder, recursive=T)

```

# Data Import

Here I load the idat files from GEO (GSE103186) from the Huang publication [Huang et al., 2018] and perform preprocssing and QC. A sample annotation was already created in  /data/projects/MB119_Methylation/analysis/Stomach_Methylation/public_data_sets/GSE103186_Huang_et_al_IM/GSE103186_Huang_et_al.Rmd  

Here, I load the ex vivo and in vivo idats and merge the data set with the healthy data set. Then, functional normalization [Fortin et al.] is applied.

```{r, fig.width=16, fig.height=8}

if(FALSE){
  sample_annotation = read.delim("../../../Data/ExtData/Other_Methylation_data/GSE103186_Huang/sample_annotation_GSE103186.csv", sep=",")

  idat_folder = "../../../Data/ExtData/Other_Methylation_data/GSE103186_Huang/Raw/IDAT"
  write.csv(sample_annotation, file.path(idat_folder, "sample_annotation.csv"), quote = F, row.names = FALSE)
  
  myLoad = champ.load(directory = idat_folder, method = "minfi")
  
  save(myLoad, file = file.path(data_storage_folder, "myLoad.RData"))
}else{
  load(file.path(data_storage_folder, "myLoad.RData"))
}
```



# Filtering

Filtered out are probes     
- with a detection p-value > 0.01  
- with a bead-count < 3  
- in which the probed CpG falls near a SNP as defined in Zhou W. *et al.*, 2016  
- in which the probe aligns to multiple locations with bwa as defined in Nordlund *et al.*, 2013   
and   
- non-cg probes  
- probes located on the X/Y chromosome

## Quality Control raw data

The QC function uses the raw beta values for initial quality control:  
- The Multidimensional Scaling Plot (MDS) visualizes the similarity of the samples based on the top 1,000 most variable probes of all samples.  
- The density Plot displays the beta distribution of each sample  
- The dendrogram clusters all samples (the distance between the samples is calculated directly by all probes)  


```{r, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}

mdsPlot(myLoad$beta, numPositions = 1000, sampGroups = myLoad$pd$Sample_Group, legendPos = "topleft", legendNCol = 1, sampNames = myLoad$pd$Site)

densityPlot(dat = myLoad$beta, sampGroups = myLoad$pd$Sample_Group, main = paste("Density plot of raw data (", nrow(myLoad$beta), " probes)", sep = ""))


  hc <- hclust(dist(t(myLoad$beta)))
  dend <- as.dendrogram(hc)
  MyColor <- rainbow(length(table(myLoad$pd$Sample_Group)))
  names(MyColor) <- names(table(myLoad$pd$Sample_Group))
  labels_colors(dend) <- MyColor[myLoad$pd$Sample_Group[order.dendrogram(dend)]]
  # dend <- dend %>% set(dend, "labels_cex", 0.7)
  # dend <- dend %>% set("leaves_pch", 19) %>% set("leaves_cex", 0.6) %>% set("leaves_col",         MyColor[myLoad$pd$Sample_Group[order.dendrogram(dend)]])
  plot(dend, center = TRUE, main = paste("All samples (", nrow(myLoad$beta), " probes)", sep = ""))
  legend("topright", fill = MyColor, legend = names(MyColor))

```

# Normalization

```{r}

if(FALSE){
  
  set.seed(123456789)

  myNorm <- champ.norm(beta = myLoad$beta, method = "SWAN", cores = 12)
  save(myNorm, file = file.path(data_storage_folder, "myNorm.RData"))

  # myNorm_funcnorm = champ.norm(method = "FunctionalNormalization", cores = 12)
  # save(myNorm_funcnorm, file = "myNorm_funcnorm.RData")
  # 
  }else{
  load(file.path(data_storage_folder, "myNorm.RData"))
  load(file.path(data_storage_folder, "myNorm_funcnorm.RData"))
}

```

## Heatmap

### SWAN

The Heatmap visualizes the similarity of the samples based on the top 1,000 most variable probes of all samples.

```{r}

o <- order(-matrixStats::rowVars(myNorm))[1:1000]
data <- myNorm[o,]
col_anno <- data.frame("Sample_Group" = myLoad$pd$Sample_Group,
                       "Site" = myLoad$pd$Site,
                       stringsAsFactors = F, row.names = myLoad$pd$Sample_Name)

pheatmap(data, cluster_rows = T, main = "Heatmap of 1,000 most variable CpGs", show_rownames = FALSE, fontsize_col = 8, annotation_col = col_anno)

```

# Batch effect correction

## SWAN

With the ChAMP SVD function (runs Singular Value Decomposition on a dataset to estimate the impact of batch effects) I test for putative batch effects. In order to correct for the slide effect that was detected in the first PC, one sample (normal corpus), which was hybridized alone to a different batch, has to be removed.

```{r}

champ.SVD(RGEffect = TRUE, beta = myNorm)


myNorm2 = myNorm[, -which(colnames(myNorm) == "GSM2756944")]
myLoad$pd = subset(myLoad$pd, myLoad$pd$Sample_Name != "GSM2756944")

if(FALSE) {


  myNorm_batch_corrected <- champ.runCombat(beta = myNorm2)

save(myNorm_batch_corrected, file = file.path(data_storage_folder, "myNorm_batch_corrected.RData"))

} else {
  load(file.path(data_storage_folder, "myNorm_batch_corrected.RData"))

}

champ.SVD(beta = myNorm_batch_corrected, RGEffect = TRUE, resultsDir = "./CHAMP_SVDimages_batch_corrected/")

```
